# Transition matrix and the probability of equal tree height

## Number of valid states

When $n > 2$, we always have $(i, j, k)$ satisfying:
$$
\begin{cases}
1 \leq i + k \leq n,\\
1 \leq j + k \leq n,\\
0 \leq i, j, k.
\end{cases}
$$
We have the number of states equals to
$$
\frac{n(2n^2 + 9n + 1)}{6}.
$$
```{r}
num_states <- function(n) {
  n * (2 * n^2 + 9 * n + 1) / 6
}

cat("n=2, num of states =", num_states(2), "\n")
cat("n=2, num of states =", num_states(3))
n_seq <- 2:20
num_seq <- num_states(n_seq)
plot(n_seq, num_seq, xlab="n", ylab="number of states")
```

## Probability of equal tree height

When $n=2$, let the tree heights to be $T_l$ and $T_c$, Simonsen and Churchill 1997 paper have their theorem 2:
$$
P(T_l = T_c) = \frac{9+\rho}{9 + 13\rho + 2\rho^2}.
$$
```{r}
prob_equal_n2 <- function(rho) {
  (9 + rho) / (9 + 13*rho + 2*rho^2)
}

rho_seq <- seq(from=0, to=20, by=0.1)
true_prob <- prob_equal_n2(rho_seq)
plot(rho_seq, true_prob, xlab="rho", ylab="P(T1 = T2)", main="n=2", type="l")
```

## Transition matrix and the probability when n > 2

The transition matrix is constructed by functions in `states_transition.R`.
```{r}
P2 <- arg_transition_matrix(2, symbolic = TRUE) # = Eq. (2)
print(noquote(unclass(P2)[, ]))
P3 <- arg_transition_matrix(3, symbolic = TRUE)
print(noquote(unclass(P3)[, ]))
```

```{r}
P2 <- arg_transition_matrix(2, rho=0.5) # = Eq. (2)
print(noquote(unclass(P2)[, ]))
P3 <- arg_transition_matrix(3, rho=1)
print(noquote(unclass(P3)[, ]))
```

When $n > 2$, we might want the probability of $\mathcal{T}_l = \mathcal{T}_c$ instead of just equal heights. Follow the proof of theorem 2, the probability is derived from $\hat{P}$. Code to compute $\hat{P}$ is in `hat_transition.R`.
```{r}
P2 <- arg_transition_matrix(2, symbolic = TRUE)
P2_hat <- transition_hat(2, P2)
print(noquote(unclass(P2_hat)[, ]))
P3 <- arg_transition_matrix(3, symbolic = TRUE)
P3_hat <- transition_hat(3, P3)
print(noquote(unclass(P3_hat)[, ]))
```

Then the probability of equal trees is computed by diagonalisation of $\hat{P}$.
```{r}
matrix_prob <- c()
for (i in 1:length(sparse_rho)) {
  rho <- sparse_rho[i]
  P <- arg_transition_matrix(2, rho=rho)
  P_hat <- transition_hat(2, P)
  eig <- eigen(P_hat)
  if (!all(abs(eig$values) <= 1)) {print("Eigenvalue larger than 1!")}
  diag_inf <- as.integer(abs(eig$values) >= 1)
  V <- eig$vectors
  D <- diag(diag_inf)
  P_hat_inf <- V %*% D %*% solve(V)
  matrix_prob <- c(matrix_prob, P_hat_inf[1, 4]) 
}

plot(rho_seq, true_prob, xlab="rho", ylab="P(T1 = T2)", main="n=2", type="l")
plot(sparse_rho, matrix_prob)
```
